description: Response header injection beyond CRLF — injecting into existing response header values (Location, Content-Type, CSP, Link, X-Frame-Options) via user-controlled input that reaches those headers without newline sanitization. Chains with XSS (Content-Type text/html), cache poisoning (Cache-Control injection), and session fixation (Set-Cookie injection).

location_header_injection.description: User input reflected in the Location header value. Beyond open redirect — injecting headers after the Location value via CRLF, or manipulating the redirect URL to include attacker-controlled fragments/parameters.

probes.description: CRLF in redirect parameter — inject a custom header after Location value
CRLF in redirect to inject Set-Cookie — session fixation via response header injection

matchers.description: Injected Set-Cookie appears in response headers

probes.description: Response splitting via CRLF — inject a complete response body with Content-Type text/html for XSS

matchers.description: Script tag reflected in response body after header injection

content_type_manipulation.description: Manipulate the Content-Type header to force browsers to interpret API responses as HTML. If user input influences the response Content-Type (e.g. via Accept header reflection, format parameter, or file extension routing), an attacker can trigger XSS on JSON/XML endpoints.

probes.description: Set format/type parameter to text/html — if reflected in Content-Type, browser renders JSON body as HTML
Append .html extension to API endpoint — some frameworks route based on extension and set Content-Type accordingly

matchers.description: Response served as text/html via extension routing

csp_injection.description: Content-Security-Policy header injection — if user input reaches the CSP header value (e.g. via a nonce, report-uri, or dynamic policy construction), an attacker can relax the policy to allow inline scripts or external script loading.

probes.description: Inject semicolon + script-src * into CSP value — if reflected, CSP is relaxed to allow all scripts

matchers.description: CSP relaxed via injection — script-src * in policy

probes.description: Inject unsafe-inline into CSP — enables inline script execution, bypassing the CSP protection entirely

matchers.description: CSP relaxed via injection — unsafe-inline in script-src

link_header_injection.description: Link header injection — inject <preload> or <prefetch> directives via user-controlled input in the Link response header. Can preload attacker-controlled scripts or exfiltrate data via DNS prefetch.

probes.description: Inject a preload Link header pointing to an attacker script — browser may preload the script

matchers.description: Attacker-controlled preload link injected into Link header
